hazards.name: Space Radiation
hazards.category: Galactic Cosmic Rays & Solar Particle Events
hazards.description: High-energy ion ionizing radiation and solar proton flux penetrating shielding, damaging cellular DNA, causing endothelial inflammation, microvascular rarefaction, and acute radiation syndrome risks.
hazards.source: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Roadmap: Risk of Radiation Carcinogenesis, CNS and Degenerative Tissue
mitigationTactics: Relocate to Storm Shelter (water-wall/polyethylene shielded core)
Administer antioxidant radioprotective countermeasures (vitamin cocktail/antioxidant)
Postpone all extravehicular activities (EVAs)
Continuous personal dosimeter monitoring

hazards.name: Isolation & Confinement
hazards.description: Extended confinement in small habitations, circadian disruption from absence of natural 24h sunlight, sensory monotony, and communication latency driving neurobehavioral fatigue and sleep architecture deterioration.
hazards.source: NASA HRP Behavioral Health & Performance (BHP) Element; Basner et al., Mars 520 Study
mitigationTactics: Enforce solid circadian dynamic lighting protocol (blue-enriched daytime, red-shifted evening)
Structured peer journaling and subjective self-assessment
Sensory stimulation (virtual reality nature simulations, earth-audio)
Scheduled mission debriefs and asynchronous family packets

hazards.name: Distance from Earth
hazards.description: Vast physical distance causing communication latencies from 2.6 seconds (Moon) up to 44 minutes (Mars opposition), eliminating real-time medical evacuation and ground surgeon telemedicine assistance.
hazards.source: NASA HRP Exploration Medical Capability (ExMC) Element: Autonomous Medical Decision Support Architecture
mitigationTactics: Execute autonomous Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs)
Utilize digital twin decision support for diagnosis
Autonomous store-and-forward telemetry buffering with high-priority packets
Independent emergency medical stabilization protocol execution

hazards.name: Altered Gravity Fields
hazards.description: Zero-G or 0.38-G (Mars) causing cephalad fluid shift (~2L shift from legs to head/thorax), bone mineral density loss (-1.2% per month in trabecular bone), sarcopenia, orthostatic intolerance, and Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS).
hazards.source: NASA-STD-3001, Vol 1: Crew Health; NASA HRP Human Physiology Countermeasures Element
mitigationTactics: Daily 2.5 hour exercise countermeasure regimen (ARED heavy load + CEVIS aerobic)
Lower Body Negative Pressure (LBNP) fluid-shift reversal sessions
Fluid and electrolyte loading prior to re-entry or gravity transitions
Visual acuity and optical coherence tomography (OCT) monitoring for SANS

hazards.name: Hostile Closed Environment
hazards.description: Artificial atmospheric containment characterized by elevated ambient CO2 levels (often 3-4 mmHg vs 0.3 mmHg on Earth), toxic trace contaminants, acoustic noise from pumps/fans, and altered microbial ecology.
hazards.source: NASA-STD-3001, Vol 2: Habitat Environments and ECLSS Specification; Law et al., Spaceflight Hypercapnia Review
mitigationTactics: ECLSS scrubber rate ramp-up to suppress partial pressure of CO2 (< 2.0 mmHg)
HEPA air filtration and airborne particulate monitoring
Active acoustic noise-cancelling headset protocol during sleep periods
Surface microbiological sanitation with space-approved quaternary biocides
